chapter: Records, dances and Blanche Calloway (repeated passages)
title: Learning to cook
summary: He learned cooking by watching his mother, sister and wife and prefers his own home cooking to restaurants.

story.theme_name: Illness, injury and the deaths of colleagues
story.community_name: Illness, injury and death among jazz musicians

blocks.x: Speaking about cooking, because that's something I wanted to ask you about... Learning to cook like you can, was that something that happened because when you were out on the road you had to sort of shift for yourself and...

Well, not exactly. I used to watch my mother cook. I used to watch her a lot, cooking, and my sister, and then I used to watch my wife cook -- she was a very cook, too. And just, you know, sometimes you have to make your own meals and things... So I started experimenting different little things, you know.
I mean, it might be good to know that sometimes, when you're out some place and you can't...
...find a good place to eat, or...

It's better. I would rather have my cooking than other people's cooking any time. I know what I'm doing. I mean, I know what I'm putting in it...everything. I prefer my own cooking. I'm sure there are some people that cook a lot better than me, and I like their cooking, but it's...it isn't (?)up near(?) no restaurant or nothin'. Home cooking. There's a few restaurants that are good, you know. Like, Chinese restaurants, I couldn't compete with that, because I don't know nothin' about Chinese... Or
Italian restaurants, I don't know much about that either. Down-to-earth cooking, things(?), you know...
